title: Automated Design Optimization via Strategic Search with Large Language Models

mechanism.domainTask: GPU code optimization for chemical kinetics and dense matrix multiplication
mechanism.populationDetail: All valid and invalid designs are added to a growing global history database; a P-best/Q-worst/R-recent subset is curated for context, with no islands or maintained genealogy.
mechanism.archiveDetail: The paper curates high-scoring designs from the accumulated database for Strategist context and reports the best result, but defines no separate persistent elite archive.
mechanism.replacementDetail: The context subset is refreshed from the growing design history; ranking affects reuse/context rather than deleting historical designs.
mechanism.generationDetail: Innovate is from-scratch, refine modifies an existing design, and combine is intended to synthesize complementary designs; concrete parent-child protocols are not fully exposed.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Detailed per-input timings and validation outcomes are retained for context. Repair-facing diagnostics are operational error feedback, not a natural-language interpretation of objective quality.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: Treat curated designs as references for the Strategist unless a direct parent relation is established; do not infer a fixed number of true parents from the combine label.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/Automated Design Optimization via Strategic Search with Large Language Models.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: The survey's current Approximate Evaluation grouping appears unsupported: the paper reports fixed benchmark input sets and compares search decisions with Bayesian optimization, but does not specify a proxy/surrogate candidate evaluator. The combine mode suggests fusion but lacks a concrete multi-parent prompt/protocol; prompt blocks are only partly exposed. Current survey coverage also omits several supported placements such as flat population, single model, and chapter-4 prompt/generation sections.
